**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant part**: Cereal leaf (wheat or similar grass crop), long and narrow
- **Color**: Predominantly green with subtle pale/chlorotic areas
- **Key features**:
  - A pale white/cream longitudinal streak visible along part of the leaf (particularly on the right side), running parallel to the leaf veins
  - Scattered small yellowish-white spots/flecks on the leaf blade
  - No obvious orange or brown pustules; no tan blotches
  - Symptoms appear early/mild with the leaf still mostly green

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Stripe Rust**: Would show yellow-orange urediniospore pustules in distinct stripes — not visible here
- **Wheat_Leaf_Rust / Stem_Rust**: Would produce circular/elongated dark orange/reddish pustules — absent
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch / Tan_Spot**: Would show tan/brown blotchy lesions with yellow halos — not matching
- **Bacterial_Leaf_Streak**: Water-soaked to tan/brown streaks bounded by veins — lesions would be darker
- **Wheat_Streak_Mosaic_Virus**: Yellow-green mosaic mottling in streaks — possible, but pattern is more diffuse here
- **Cephalosporium_Stripe**: Causes distinctive white to pale-yellow stripes running longitudinally along the full leaf length, caused by a soilborne fungus (Cephalosporium gramineum). The pale/white linear streak and scattered chlorotic spots on an otherwise green cereal leaf match this profile well.

The longitudinal pale/white stripe running parallel to the veins, combined with subtle scattered chlorosis on a cereal leaf, is most characteristic of **Cephalosporium Stripe**.
